digest.component_or_area: code-review criteria — tests and error-handling reviewers
propositions: A check that asserts absence (empty output, no match, missing value) on subprocess or file-read output with no producer-liveness verification cannot distinguish pass from producer failure, creating a fail-open oracle defect.

The same broken instrument can produce a false positive verdict (confident fail result for a reason other than the condition), inverted from the fail-open (silent pass) case, and is equally undistinguishable from instrument failure.

The fail-open producer-liveness language must be added to both the existing tests criterion (test-oracle population) and error-handling criterion (shipped-code population) rather than create a new criterion, with language, FP guards, and calibration corpus distributed across both rubrics.

Nine pre-recorded calibration instances across test code and shipped code (pgrep self-matches, grep without returncode checks, silent lookup misses, signal-killed child outputs, truncated logs, unchecked return statuses) must yield ≥1 grounded finding naming the seeded defect when replayed against pre-fix diffs, and zero findings against post-fix diffs.
